enumeration._one_widget_per_field: 447 fields and 447 widgets with none unplaced, so on this form no field is drawn twice. That is worth asserting rather than assuming: f433d.pdf draws every one of its 84 leaf stems TWICE, and a map binding by stem there writes to the taxpayer copy.

Its 103 resolve into five structural blocks, derived from the subform tree and the printed markers: Section 1 left column (Line1a-f, 11 cells, markers 1a to 1f), Section 1 right column (2a to 3d and line 4, 16 cells), the payment-processor table (Table_Line5a-b, 4 cells, markers 5a and 5b), the credit-card table (Table_Lines6a-c, 12 cells, markers 6a to 6c) and Section 2's four personnel rows (Line7a_Col1 to Line7d_Col1, 15 cells each, markers 7a to 7d). 11 + 16 + 4 + 12 + 60 = 103.

checkbox_probe._the_on_states_are_NOT_uniform_on_this_f: 13 distinct on-states, and that is the finding. 433-B(OIC) turns every one of its 77 boxes on with /1 and a map for it can carry one spelling; this form cannot. Page 1's 2b entity list alone uses /Partnership, /Corporation, /Other, /LLC and /Other#20LLC; the question pairs use /Yes and /No; page 5 uses /Secured and /Unsecured and /Plaintiff and /Defendent; page 6 uses /Cash and /Accrual. A fill engine that wrote /1 here would tick nothing and report success, which is why the on-state is read from the widget rather than assumed.
checkbox_probe._the_IRS_spells_one_of_them_Defendent: Page 5 stores /Defendent, not /Defendant. It is written as it is stored. A map that corrected the spelling would silently tick nothing.
checkbox_probe._the_one_with_an_escape_in_it: /Other#20LLC — the on-state of topmostSubform[0].Page1[0].c1_0_2b[4] carries a PDF name-object escape for a space. It must be written as it is stored, not as "Other LLC".

lineage._the_question_it_answers: Which of this form's AcroForm leaf names are inherited from a form already in this engine, and per OCCURRENCE whether this form's printed caption matches, contradicts, or asks a new question under that name.
lineage._the_rule_it_is_read_under: An inherited leaf name is evidence of nothing. A verdict is per occurrence, never per name — which this form demonstrates twice over: `p2_t11_13a` matches on one of its three occurrences and contradicts on the other two.
lineage._every_occurrence_is_on_one_page: All 17 sit on page 3. PAGE 1 — the page this slice maps — CARRIES NOT ONE INHERITED LEAF NAME. Every name on it is this form's own.
lineage._the_headline: THE LINEAGE IS INERT, AND IT IS INERT BY CONSTRUCTION RATHER THAN BY LUCK. Name-lie registries exist on 433-A(OIC) (31 entries) and 433-B(OIC) (37), and this form shares ZERO leaf names with either. The 11 names it does share are shared with 433-A and 433-F, and neither of those has a registry. So the intersection of "shared with a form" and "carries a registry entry" is EMPTY — no entry in any registry in this tree stands on any name this form inherits, and nothing is inherited into 433-B's own registry when it is opened.
lineage._and_that_is_the_opposite_of_the_OIC_lin: 433-B(OIC) shares 83 leaf names with 433-A(OIC), 9 of which carry registry entries, and three of those names are true on one page of 433-B(OIC) and false on another. The two lineages are almost disjoint: the OIC forms inherit from each other and 433-B inherits from the non-OIC pair. A registry is not a thing this engine has that applies to every form; it is a thing that follows a lineage.

inherited_guards_during_intake._the_question: Which guards this engine already carried FIRED on this new form, and which did not. A guard that never fires on new input has not been tested on new input.
_fired: adapters/pdf/correlate-labels.mjs probe self-check — REFUSED to write a labels file. Three pairings established from the printed page and this tool answered the caption one row ABOVE on all three. See [B-01]. This is the guard doing exactly what it was written for: a form with no probes is refused, and a form whose probes fail produces no artefact.

adapters/pdf/line-markers.mjs under-determination report — 113 printed markers, 101 with a widget on the same row, and it declares 85 of those 101 pairings UNDER-DETERMINED: more than one widget survived its geometric filter and a distance tie-break chose. It states that the choice is the tool's and not the page's, which is [N-05]'s remedy actually implemented.
